text_translated_detailed:
Memorandum of everything that was used and provided for the construction, fitting out, and equipping of the new Chaloup [small vessel] named Aletta Adriana, measuring 72 feet in length, 22 feet in width, 10½ feet in depth, and of 50 lasts [modern equivalent: approximately 100 tons] capacity; namely by those of the shipyard:

3 pieces of Dutch mast timber, of which 1 piece of 21½ palms [modern equivalent: approximately 16-17 feet] in length, cost ƒ 386.5.—; 1 piece of 12 palms in length, cost ƒ 61.16.—; 1 piece of 14 palms in length, cost ƒ 72.2.—; 1 piece of unfinished wang [uncertain: possibly a specific timber type]; 1 piece of spier or underpalm, cost ƒ 4.3.—. 25 pieces of large Lincan planks at ƒ 3.13.3. per piece, cost ƒ 91.10.—; 19 pieces of small ones at ƒ 15.5. per piece, cost ƒ 14.11.—; 16 pieces of Batavian assorted swallows [uncertain: possibly a timber type], cost ƒ 10.11.—

text_original: Dewyl het jaarlykse Examen der Qreekelingen van het Seminanium alhier, om de wille der langduurige ziekte en uyterste zwakheid des eersten Teekenaars dezes als Rector daar van niet kan worden gehouden, dat anderzints het veertiende zyns Rectoraats zyn zoude, zoo heeft hy zig neffens den tweeden Teekenaar als Conrector van dat Qneekschool verpligt geagt hier onder beknoptelyk en zeffens naa waarheid op te geeven, wat er deezen Jaare met de meer metde Arackelingen is getracteert geworden, en hoe verre deselve in hunne Letteroeffeningen gevorderd zyn By den eersten Teekenaar als Rector, hebben de vier volgende Queekelingen, namentlyk. G Hendrik Philipsz. Lingalees. Mosties Pieter Cornelisz Mallebaar, en Jurij Ondatje Willem — Bastiaan Jansz Mallebaar getractaerd veram Logieam, sen Priman Philosophiam die in 't gemeen genaamd word Metaphysica, en zulk volgens haare Lres partes, Pneumatica, Theologia Naturalis et Rysica Generalis; Secundum met hodum Coenradi Mel. Hebbende hy hen daar uijt Locos in calamum gedieteerd, ja zelfs Paragraphos en Pa ginas aangeweezen. Bezonders zijn de gemelde scholieren g oeffend in Cormandis et reducendis syllogismis, en de drie een ste om dies wille bequaam geoordeeld, de Lectiones Mcademicas met nut en voordeel te konnen frequenteeren; waar en tegen de laatste een subject is, dat men in allen deelen zeer straf en hard behan delen moet, waaromme men dan ook niet reeden geene verwagting van hem hebben kan dat hij ad altiora Andia zal konnen worden gebragt. De reeds benoemde vier Queekelingen zyn door den tweeden Teekenaar ook onderweezen in Vossu Proceptis Rhetoricis, insgelyjks hebben ze drationes Ciceronis et Terontium g'exponeert, en zyn in Analysi groca N: T: geaeffent. Voorts zyn onder het onderwys van den tweden Tekenaar geweest: Philip Jurgiaan Ondatje Mallebaar, Andreas Spoor . . . . Misties; welke hebben Gicero„ nem et Proedri Fabulas g'exponeert, Cornelium Nepotein et syntaxin gerepeteert, Themata gemaakt
text_translated_detailed: Since the annual examination of the pupils of the Seminary here cannot be held on account of the prolonged illness and extreme weakness of the first Teacher thereof as Rector, which would otherwise be the fourteenth of his Rectorship, he has deemed it necessary, together with the second Teacher as Co-rector of that school, to provide herunder a concise and truthful account of what has been done this year with the pupils, and how far they have advanced in their literary exercises. Under the instruction of the first Teacher as Rector, the following four pupils, namely G. Hendrik Philipsz. Lingalees, Mosties Pieter Cornelisz. Mallebaar, and Jurij Ondatje Willem—Bastiaan Jansz. Mallebaar, have been instructed in Logic and First Philosophy, which is commonly called Metaphysics, and accordingly in its three parts, Pneumatics, Natural Theology, and General Physics; secondly in the method of Coenrad Mel. He has dictated to them passages into their notebooks, indeed even indicated paragraphs and pages. text_translated_detailed: Report of the General Visitation of the Native Churches and Schools under the Colombo District, begun the 20th of July and concluded the 15th of September in the year 1751, by the Preacher 135.—222. Sigisbertus Abrahamsz. Bronsveld, and the under-merchant and Scholarch Huijbert Hoogerwaard, respectfully presented to the well-esteemed, greatly honored, high commanding Lord Gerrard Ioan Vrielandt, Extraordinary Councillor of the Netherlands Indies, as well as Governor and Director of the Island of Ceylon and its dependencies. Well-esteemed, greatly honored, high commanding Lord! Since it has pleased your well-esteemed great honor to entrust to us the visitation of the native churches and schools under this district, we take the liberty to bring before your well-esteemed great honor, in all humility, a truthful account of our proceedings and findings, in the hope that this may be graciously received by the same. First, may it please your well-esteemed great honor to note that we, in the execution of our commission, have maintained the same procedure as was customarily used of old, insofar as circumstances permitted, performing in some of the smaller schools the entire service of the morning, but in the larger schools holding the administration of Holy Baptism and the solemnization of marriage until the afternoon. The time at which our service began daily was at nine or half past nine o'clock; however, as soon as the people had gathered together and the roll-keeper had completed the preliminaries, consisting of the taking of attendance and regulation of the present schoolchildren. The first Teacher of this place, as soon as he had arrived at a location, demanded from the schoolmaster a neat list, not only of all the Christians and of the schoolchildren, but especially also of those who had offered their children for Holy Baptism or themselves for marriage

Noble and greatly esteemed sir, how we have conducted ourselves in visiting and serving the 46 native schools under this Colombo district, hoping that your noble and greatly esteemed [sir] will graciously approve of this conduct. Now as to our findings, on the one hand we have abundant reasons to thank God that there are still many found among this native Christianity who have some desire for knowledge of God's ways and to accept the offered salvation, but on the other hand we are compelled, though otherwise reluctant, to grieve over the lamentable state of those poor and blind Christians. For when we carefully examine the school-going youth, their lack of progress in most schools corresponds entirely to the sluggish school attendance, of which the causes have been variously given to us. For when we asked most of the schoolmasters how such a poor state of progress should be found, one gave us the prevailing poverty among the native people, another the persistent sicknesses in the land, a third the disobedience and stubbornness of the children, and a fourth the wicked unwillingness of the others, as reasons for the children's absence. text_translated_detailed: in particular since such a God and honor-forsaken man would not have feared great extremities, we, at the request of the inhabitants there, sent him to Caliture to await the esteemed orders of your Noble Excellency there, while we meanwhile heard his lawful wife testify that this godless deed had been made known to her by his own brother, her young brother-in-law, which she, having notified her mother thereof, also found to constitute a great and unworthy mistreatment of the man, in that she was not only treated by him with blows and kicks, but was also reproached together with her mother that, saving reverence, he had dishonored her two unmarried daughters. All of which we have not only made known to your Noble Excellency in our humble writings at that time, but also deem it necessary to humbly present in this our respectful report. On Aligam it appeared to us in particular very poorly, both the advancement of the children as well as the conduct of the schoolmasters. Which we must likewise note of the school Baddoegodde, where to our astonishment it appeared to us that the thombo [register] is entirely defective, as very many names of households were found to be absent therein. The schoolmasters defended themselves by saying that while the previous schoolmaster had betaken himself to Colombo with his thombo, through the breaking of the thread with which the classes were bound together, several pages had been lost. When we remarked upon this, we had to obtain as an answer why the present schoolmasters had not made this known to the Reverend scholarchale [school council] gathering, that they had neglected to do so, because the former thombo-keeper Caldera had promised them that he would supply those lost names anew, which seemed to us entirely improper and irregular.

At Welligampittie, where we found the school service satisfactory, upon leaving the school we had to receive from the vidaan [local official] a complaint letter against the conduct of the schoolmasters, just as we also received a response from the schoolmasters afterward, both of which we respectfully present to Your Noble Excellency herewith, and concerning which we could provide further information to Your Noble Excellency if it should please you. At Dandoegam, the house prepared for the proponent Abraham Pieris has not only not been brought into readiness until now, but has also been partly demolished again through the negligence of the vidaan, and it is also everywhere full of white ants, whereby it is impossible for the proponent to dwell in it as yet; wherefore we respectfully request Your Noble Excellency that the necessary orders might be given thereto. text_translated_detailed: whereby this legitimate schoolmaster, who also declared himself willing for that service, was deprived of school children, requesting therefore that he be maintained according to all church order in this matter, and that the others be forbidden to hold any unlawful schools henceforth, or to draw school children from the Company's schools to themselves: which, under favorable consideration and upon free approval of your Well-Born Great Esteemed [Excellency], was granted to him, and the aforementioned Consumption-bookkeeper I requested to keep a watchful eye over this school and school service, as well as over the instruction of this schoolmaster, in the future. However, since this sick-visitor and precentor of the Dutch language and writing is not yet sufficiently skilled, I gave the lord Salder the choice, whether he would retain the dismissed precentor in the meantime, to assist the sick-visitor in the school service, until it might please your Well-Born Great Esteemed [Excellency] to decide on this matter as you see fit; although the diligence and zeal of the frequently mentioned sick-visitor is great, and his conduct, so far as I have been able to ascertain, is blameless. I also examined the books, both of the school, which are quite scanty and insufficient, as well as of the church; and in the latter I found that the precentor does not hesitate to deliver a sermon composed by himself against all church order in public, often to the offense of the congregation, but I pointed out to him in a friendly manner that he should refrain from this in the future, and according to custom read a sermon from the book of van der Hagen each week, since the nature of his office permits this alone, and it is likewise the means to maintain orthodoxy and peace in the church. Furthermore, I recommended to him to resume the service on Sunday afternoons according to old custom, but submitting myself to the wise judgment and favorable disposition of your Well-Born Great Esteemed [Excellency], as well as whether it might please your Well-Born Great Esteemed [Excellency] to graciously approve the appointment of the elder Abraham François Emans— proceeding from here to the indigenous Christianity, I have the honor to respectfully inform your Well-Born Great Esteemed [Excellency] that I conducted the school visitation in the Malabar school there, in the presence of the Calpettij council, on the 12th or Tuesday, and found that the number of Christians belonging to that church, according to the statement of the schoolmaster, consists of 271 persons, or 132 men and 139 women, among whom 22 schoolboys and 15 schoolgirls are found. These were little or not at all practiced in the common prayers and catechisms, since only three boys were found who could recite a catechism, while the others at most could recite the Lord's Prayer, the twelve articles, and the ten commandments, but very imperfectly. Having brought this great decline and neglect of the school service to the schoolmaster's attention, the same was attributed by the schoolmaster to the school children and their parents, but by the lord Salder to the negligence of the schoolmaster, the aforementioned lord declaring that the school, since my departure from there in the year 1749, had not been opened until 14 days before my present arrival there. After completing the visitation in the schools, having questioned the schoolmaster about this unforgivable neglect, I had to receive as an answer that he had received just such a list of names and ages from the hands of the previous schoolmaster, and had directed himself according to that example. I have deemed it necessary to instruct the schoolmaster, with the favorable approval of your Noble Excellency, to send his school baptismal register to Colombo, in order to compare it with the Dutch baptismal register resting here, and to correct it according to the same. Nevertheless we must say, having heard it with astonishment, that one has given Your Excellency's Esteemed Authority favorable reports about these pig sties, as if they were buildings in which the principal persons on this island need not be ashamed to take up residence and lodging, and that we cannot regard it otherwise than as driving his own work somewhat in his own interest. The teaching or instruction of youth at these schools is also not very abundant and quite poor at Eloedoematuaal, although here and there in the surrounding area various girls are found who, just as the boys elsewhere, diligently practice themselves in prayers and catechisms, and indeed often are able to recite some chapters from Matthew. Having thus briefly spoken of the state of Singhalese Christianity in general, we shall, before we proceed to the particular examination of the schools, first make Your Reverence understand how we have proceeded in the handling of matters. Upon arriving at a place where a school was to be visited, the bookkeeper must enroll the school according to the roll of schoolchildren which he receives from the headmaster, arranging the children according to that made roll into catechumens with catechumens, and that indeed mostly the most advanced at the top and then in succession. Secondly, the minister and schoolmaster then go to the school, where according to the circumstances of the time, either with the customary morning prayer or with the Lord's Prayer, which one of the most practiced schoolchildren must recite, and the examination begins. The school building here has deteriorated to such a degree that it no longer deserves the name of school, being not only open on all sides but also covered with glass that is completely rotten, so that no one is able to shelter themselves here from the sun or rain, and complaints about the deterioration of this school have already been made for several years. text_translated_detailed: School. There belong to it 101 schoolchildren, both boys and girls, of which 52 are in the first class and among these 17 were late catechumens. The school children are here, each according to their ability, exercised with good success in spelling, reading, writing, praying, in the Heidelberg Catechism, in the Small Catechism, in Lingen [uncertain: possibly a text or location name]. text_translated_detailed: Thus, the visiting of the schools being completed, we have only briefly to report concerning the state of the congregation of this place, that one has in the same 134 Dutch communicants and approximately 24 Sinhalese communicants. text_translated_detailed: The principal reason for this is that the monetary penalties, which previously were imposed on those who neglected church and school attendance, as well as on those living in a state of concubinage, have now been abolished. This has had the effect among the careless people that they have since that time concerned themselves little or not at all with church and school attendance. One gives this into consideration whether it would not be better if those penalties were reintroduced on the former footing. It is true that true Christianity does not wish to be propagated by force or by compulsion, but it is on the other hand also true that a Sinhalese, almost in no matter, can be moved to fulfill his duty without threat and without compulsion. We do not regard the monetary penalties as a means of force to compel them to convert to Christianity, but only as a means that should give the Sinhalese occasion to fulfill his duty regarding Christianity, which serves for the salvation of their souls. And we also cannot regard the Sinhalese, although aged, as those who have come to the full use of their understanding, but as children who must continually be kept under the rod of discipline due to lack of understanding. And indeed among the Sinhalese, when we compare them with our cultivated European people, we find but little reasonable action in the soul.

text_translated_detailed: We give this into consideration of our Illustrious superiors, and we shall await their good judgment thereupon with patience. Meanwhile we further wish that God Almighty would pour out richly upon our Illustrious superiors the spirit of wisdom, of knowledge, of counsel, and of understanding. May He bless all their counsels, and in particular those which might be taken for the support of that so very declining Christendom. May He make their government all-seeing, so that they may show themselves not only as examples of true godliness, but also as leaders of the Lord's church, through whose efforts the kingdom of Jesus may be extended. But in particular, Your Esteemed Sir, may God Almighty take you into His gracious protection, fill you with His spirit, endow you with all necessary spiritual and bodily strength, and make you faithful in that post in which His Divine providence has placed you, so that justice and righteousness may be maintained in the land, and we under our vine and fig tree may enjoy the good of the land. This we wish with heart and soul, understanding Your Esteemed and well-commanding Sir! Your Esteemed very humble and obedient servants, signed A. F. Schultze and C. van Dam. In the margin: Gale, the 5th of September.

On the 4th of March there came to this roadstead the English Company's ship named Heu, coming from Bengal, lying at the roadstead as commander Willem Rob, manned with 120 men, provisioned with 30 pieces of cannon, the same saluted the castle with 15 shots, which were followed with 13 of the same from the ship Amstelveen, being laden with rice, whose master appearing on shore requested to be furnished with some barrels of drinking water, and these were obtained and taken on board, moreover 3,000 sacks of that potash having been sold to private parties, so the same undertook the journey to Surat on the 12th of that month. On the 30th of December there let drop anchor in the inner roadstead a two-masted brigantine named Johanna Elisabeth, commanded by Captain Joan White Leblancq, belonging to the Honorable lord Bengal director Johannes Kerseboom, which on the 26th of April 1751 again departed toward the Coast of Coromandel, after having purchased from the Honorable Company 91 ammonams of areca. On the 18th of April there arrived in the inner bay the private French ship named Delamaar, commanded by Captain Letermellier, coming from Bengal and destined toward the Maldives, but the same had to put in at this haven because the monsoon had passed and it also lacked drinking water, with which its sailors were furnished, after the sale of 80 lasts [modern equivalent: approximately 80,000 kg] of rice in 1751 to private parties, without negotiating anything from the Company, on the 5th of May of that month undertaking the return journey toward the aforementioned direction. At Trincomalee. On the 9th of December there came to anchor there two English Company's ships named Severn and a private vessel named Mamadia, the first commanded by Captain Richard Dovill and the other by Captain James Barton, where after the same had taken on the Chincosen negotiated there, on the 12th of that month they left the bay and their course was set toward Nagapatnam. At Tutucorijn in 1751 on the 18th of May there let drop anchor at the outer roadstead a certain English sloop named Louiza, commanded by Captain Richard Dodge, coming from Anssenga and destined toward Bengal, of 50 tons, manned with 12 men and laden with planks, coir rope and rope, but the same, after the first, after the purchase by its sailors of refreshments and other necessities, chose the sea again. Colombo, the last day of August, in the year 1751. Reviewed by Willem Ven, Esq., accorded by J. V. Cuijlenburg. E. Clercq.

Well Noble, Strict, highly esteemed, wise, provident, and most Generous Lords. text_translated_detailed: since we have provided the necessary assignments to those interested on our part, we humbly request that the aforementioned amount, as shown in the memorandum enclosed herein, may be paid through the kindness of your Noble Highness in the Netherlands. Likewise, we request that your Noble Highness graciously deign to dispose favorably of three Petitions by Client van Seelst of Amsterdam, bookkeeper, and Pieter Stricht, blacksmith of Amsterdam, hospital attendant, in the service of your Noble Highness, now under this government, and by one Helena de Ridder, widow of the aforementioned carpenter named Jan Paulusz van Halsouw, who died here some time ago, directed to your Noble Highness, and for the sake of the Supplicants, considerable authority with us for transmission under our humble intercession accepted, most humbly begging that they may be relieved of certain monthly portions that painfully burden her, which, if she can demonstrate them, have long since fallen due and should have been deducted, yet in the Indies remain in full force to her debit, as well as that to the Supplicants may be returned and allowed to enjoy all such monthly payments as have been withheld from the aforementioned monthly accounts since the time of expiration, but have not occurred and thus have remained to her benefit as a credit. Finally, may your Noble Highness deign to receive here a packet with advice from the Cochin ministers sent hither this day in order that it not yet be sent by this ship. And for the rest, having nothing further to add here than our sincere wish that Heaven may graciously bless the interests of the general company which we serve, as well as your Noble Highness's illustrious persons ever more abundantly, we conclude and remain with deep respect. Het vierde off laatste retourschip Spaane „derswout tans mede zeilvaardig „leggende om de reyse naart liev Vaderland te onderneemen, zo neem ik de Vrijheid in desen gesloten uw hoog Edele groot agtb. aan te presenteeren, niet alleen een Korte factuur van het afgeladene in gemelte bodem pro patria, maer ook het afschrift mijner humbel schrijvens, welk ik het geluk hade per de Iongst vertrokkene naschepen Bloemendaal en saamslag aan uw hoog Edele groot agtb. te laten afgaan, Wenschende dat het een en ander van derselver genoegen mag bevonden werden. ondertussen geeff ik mij de hoge Eere, met diepschuldig respect desen te onderteikenen als. Wel Edele groot achtb: wijdgebiedende en seer genereuse Heeren! uwel Edele groot achtb: onderdanige en gehoorsamen dienaar. Colombo den 22 Januarij 1752. G„ Jr Rreelandt
text_translated_detailed: Amsterdam. To the Well-born, Most Esteemed Gentlemen Philips van der Ghiessen, Josua van der Poorten, and Leendert Bomme, Representatives of His Serene Highness the Prince of Orange and Nassau, &c., &c., at the Assembly of the Seventeen of the general Dutch East India Company. Well-born, most esteemed, widely governing and most generous Gentlemen! The fourth or last return ship Spaanderswout, now likewise lying ready to sail to undertake the voyage to our dear Fatherland, so I take the liberty herein to present to your Noble Highness not only a brief invoice of the cargo loaded in the aforementioned vessel for the homeland, but also a copy of my humble letter, which I had the good fortune to send to your Noble Highness by the recently departed ships Bloemendaal and Saamslag, wishing that both may be found to your satisfaction. Meanwhile, I give myself the high honor, with deep respectful submission, to sign this as. Well-born, most esteemed, widely governing and most generous Gentlemen! Your Noble Highness's obedient and respectful servant. Colombo, the 22nd of January 1752. G. Jr. Reeland.

text_translated_detailed: To the Well-born, Esteemed Gentlemen, Directors of the general Dutch chartered East India Company at the chamber in Amsterdam. Esteemed Gentlemen. Although we hope that our respectful last letters of the 10th of this month, sent by Bloemendaal and Saamslag, will reach your Noble Highness safely, through a fortunate arrival of those vessels, we nevertheless send this duplicate for greater peace of mind, under respectful communication that the ship Spaanderswout, destined for your Noble Highness's chamber, brings herewith a divided cargo, being the customary one-third for the chamber of Zeeland, whose previously departed companions under God's guidance now come to follow, the cargo amounting to ƒ 355,102.8 [Dutch guilders], and together with the cargoes of the three preceding vessels, totaling a considerable sum of ƒ 1,145,734.16 [Dutch guilders]. And since we, in order to lose no time, have ordered according to custom that all the ship and business documents belonging hereto be sent directly to your Noble Highness from there, we take the liberty to conduct ourselves accordingly. Likewise, regarding what is dealt with in our separately enclosed respectful letters of today's date to the assembly of the Seventeen at your Noble Highness's chamber, Colombo, the 22nd of January. Meurilen, V. Bles. Meanwhile, for the rest, commending your Noble Highness's dear persons and the Company's important interests to God's keeping and wishing the bearer hereof a fortunate and safe voyage, we remain with dutiful respect. Esteemed Gentlemen, your Noble Highness's most obedient and respectful servants. G. J. V. Erdelard, A. Goo, W. D. Schmeling, Cramer, A. W. Berghuijs.

text_translated_detailed: To the Esteemed and Honorable Lord Fredrik Cunes, Commander of the City and Lands of Gale, Mataram, &c. Esteemed and Honorable Commanding Lord! In fulfillment of Your Esteemed Honorable gracious order contained in written ordinance dated the 27th of this month, we undersigned Steven Bade, Captain Lieutenant and Equipment Master, Hendrik Leendertsz., and Cornelis Decker Pilots, together with Jan Booij boatswain from the shore, have jointly proceeded on board the return ship Spaanderswoud [Spaanderswoud], which is currently anchored in this bay, and there in the presence of the commanding skipper Pieter Tornbohm, we have exactly and carefully inspected the standing rigging of the vessel and found that the main yard is unfit [uncertain: onbeq:]; therefore a new one of the same is required. And in like manner the passage [uncertain: Pagssisie] running rigging, which is likewise worn and unfit, so a new one was required for that as well. And since this vessel is only provided with five heavy ropes, so also five more of the same must be supplied to it, as according to the order for the homeward voyage one is too few, the remaining standing rope work of this keel being found to be good and serviceable, so that under the Lord's blessing, the voyage to the fatherland can be undertaken with peace of mind. With which we hope to have satisfied Your Esteemed Honorable gracious intention, we sign ourselves with deep respect, [undersigned] Esteemed Honorable Commanding Lord, Your Esteemed Honorable obedient Servants [was signed] I. n Baade, a cross, therefore signed, this is the mark of Hendrik Leenderts, a cross, therefore signed, this is the mark of Cornelis Dekker, and Jan Booij, in the margin Gale the 29th December 1751, [lower] [in my presence] [signed] Pieter Tornboom. e Heylinck. To the Esteemed and Honorable Lord Fredrik Cunes, Commander of the City and Lands of Gale, Mataram. Esteemed and Honorable Commanding Lord! In accordance with Your Esteemed Honorable gracious command contained in written ordinance

Ending herewith the attestants their given declaration, which they testify to contain the upright and pure truth, giving as reason for knowledge as in the text, over which they remain ready to make the attested matter good further with oath. Thus done and passed in the city of Gale [Galle:], at the secretariat of police and justice, on the day, month and year aforesaid, in the presence of Hendrik Carolus Jansz: and Cornelis Smittenberg, clerks as witnesses, who have signed the minute of this together with the attestants and me, First Sworn Clerk. Clement Van Seelst, van Amsterdam Boekhouder in dienst der Edele maatscappij, Request gepresenteert, aan de Ceijlonse Regeering, ter ontheffing van een maandceel, zoo is goedgunstiglijk den Suppliant geaccorde zig bij Requesten, van Uwel Edel gestrenge Groot Agtbaare, de Heeren Bewinthebberen te addresseeren, ter Camer waarvoo hij suppliant is uijtgevaaren, zoo gieft den zelven demoedig en in Schuld Eerbiedigheijt te kennen, dat den Jupp in 't Iaar 1744. in de maant Junij voor de Camer Amsterdam Per het schip Diemermeer, v derde waak is uijtgevaare, en een maandceel Gemaakt op mijne mo Anna Geertruijda Cochiu die voor mijn vertrek uijt Amsterdam is komen te overlijden, en den zelven Bevooren Verkogt, aan den Boekb van 't oostindische huijs, in name Hendrik Bosch, en dat voor een Jaar, als dan doot en de temel wesen Zoude, het welk bij een notar is beschreven, N: N: en tot heeden nog op de Zenne berust, en Continueert, dierhalven bid, en smeekt den supp:t uwel Edele Gestrenge groot agtb: om die maandceel herwaarts te senden, of Extirpateuren, op dat den supp:t, sijne te goet hebbende, en de volle gagie mag genieten; tot nodig onderhout sijner Economi, voor soo een weldaat, sal den Supp:t met Eijver tragten, sijnes Levens Erkentelijk en Dankbaar Tezijn. Era Pra Gra T welk Doende Ed:l Ed:e Elc:e Clement Van Seelst. N„s N„s Lebeck Aan de Wel Edele Gestrenge Heeren, Philips Van der Ghiessen, en Josua
text_translated_detailed:
From Lebeck [Galle]
To the Well-Honored, Strict, and Esteemed Gentlemen Philips van der Giesen, Josua van der Poorten, and Leendert Bomme, Representatives of His Serene Highness the Lord Prince of Orange and Nassau, Etc., Etc., Etc., and the Honored, Highly Esteemed Gentlemen Directors, at the meeting of the Seventeen of the General Dutch East India Company, at the Chamber Amsterdam.

Well-Honored, Strict, Highly Esteemed, Wise, Prudent, and Most Generous Gentlemen,

Clement Van Seelst, of Amsterdam, Bookkeeper in the service of the Honored Company, having presented a Request to the Ceylon Government for the remission of a monthly portion, it has been graciously granted to the Supplicant [petitioner] that he address himself by Request to Your Well-Honored, Strict, Highly Esteemed Gentlemen Directors at the Chamber for which the Supplicant departed, thus he gives humbly and in dutiful respect to know that the Supplicant in the year 1744, in the month of June, departed for the Chamber Amsterdam by the ship Diemermeer, in the third week, and made a monthly portion in the name of my mother Anna Geertruijda Cochiu, who before my departure from Amsterdam came to pass away, and the same was previously sold to the Bookkeeper of the East Indian house, in the name Hendrik Bosch, and that for one year, as then death and the entire matter would be, which was described by a notary, N.N., and until today still rests on the Seine [uncertain: possibly a reference to a location or document], and continues, therefore I beg and beseech the Supplicant Your Well-Honored, Strict, Highly Esteemed to send that monthly portion hither, or to appoint Executors, so that the Supplicant, having his due, and may enjoy the full wages; for the necessary support of his household, for such a benefaction, the Supplicant shall endeavor with zeal to be grateful and thankful for the rest of his life.

Era Pra Gra T [uncertain: abbreviation, possibly ceremonial closing]
Which doing, Honored, Honored, Each [uncertain: abbreviation]
Clement Van Seelst.
N.N. [uncertain: abbreviation]

Lebeck

To the Well-Honored, Strict Gentlemen Philips Van der Ghiessen and Josua van der Poorten, Representatives of His Serene Highness the Lord Prince of Orange and Nassau, &c., &c., &c., and the Honored, Highly Esteemed Gentlemen Directors at the Meeting of the Seventeen of the General Dutch East India Company, at the Chamber Amsterdam.

Well-Honored, Strict, Highly Esteemed, Wise, Prudent, and Most Generous Gentlemen!

Pieter Strigt of Amsterdam, sick visitor at the Command of Gale [Galle], Your Well-Honored, Strict, Most Humble and Obedient Servant, gives with prior knowledge and upon the obtained favorable permission of the Highly Venerated Government of this Island Ceylon, in all submission with deep respect to know: how the Supplicant in the year 1735, at the Chamber Amsterdam, was accepted as a Sick Comforter in the service of the Honored Company, and that year arrived in India with the ship de Vis, having at that time upon his appointment, in the name of the Supplicant's mother Jacomijntje Joseph (who was already deceased at that time) three months set aside, with the intention to be able to save something from his earned monthly wages for his old age, and the same upon returning to Europe to receive himself, as Your Well-Honored, Strict Gentlemen will possibly know that such is practiced more often by the Honored Company's servants, as by this means their passage is cut off from being able to take up everything in the Land; but considering, Well-Honored, Strict Gentlemen, the Supplicant on his return journey from Batavia with the return ship The House at Marquette in the year 1737, coming to port at Gale [Galle], had the misfortune of breaking his leg, and through this heavy Misfortune had to remain behind from the homeward journey, whereupon he then, according to the good judgment of the Supplicant's respected superiors and commanders on this Island, was installed here in the aforementioned capacity and remained, with the guidance of the Almighty, after this date in these regions also married, and in that married state by God Almighty blessed with a daughter, who has now reached the age of 10 years, and the Supplicant over such in this difficult time is in great need of the still owed pension of the aforementioned Monthly Deed for the support of his household with wife and child, &c.; thus he Supplicant begs Your Well-Honored, Strict, Most Humbly, that it please Your Honors out of consideration of the alleged reasons to graciously deign to have the still owed monthly wages regarding the aforementioned arrangement paid out to the Supplicant's appointed representative in Amsterdam (being a Nephew of the Supplicant, named Pieter Brouwer) under proper receipt, and to have this burdensome arrangement graciously struck off, and thereafter as the same shall provide himself for that purpose (provided with a secretarial power of attorney, dated the 6th of September, Anno 1751, before the Bookkeeper and first sworn Clerk of Police and Justice of this city Gale, Gerrit de

Well-honored, esteemed, highly respected, wise, prudent, and most generous gentlemen! The petitioner herein, Helena de Ridder, widow and estate administrator of the under-carpenter Jan Palusz of Halsouw (who in the year 1736 arrived here for the Amsterdam chamber with the ship Het Huijs te Marquette and died on the 28th of August 1750), respectfully requests your well-honored and highly esteemed Honors that it may please your well-honored and highly esteemed Honors to have the money remaining to her husband's credit in the fatherland regarding a certain monthly allowance that was arranged for the benefit of his first wife and which, by reason of her death in the year 1736, ceased to be paid to his authorized agent, the gentleman Aren Assing, baker, residing on the corner of the Utrecht cross-street at the inner Amstel in Amsterdam, be paid out; whereby the poor and needy petitioner can be placed in a position to pay the remaining legitimate debt of the aforementioned her husband.

text_original: Heeden den 27e: November A„o 1751. Compareerde voor mij Gerrit De vos, boekhouder en Eerste gesw: Clercq dezes gaalsen Commandements, present de naerbesz: getuijgen d E: Jan willemsz: van den Briel Capit=n Lieuten=t n Benjamin Carool lieutenant beijft in die qualiteijten bescheijden op het indees baaij zeijlvaerdig leggende retourschip Zuijderburg, dewelke te samen en een ieder van hen in het bijsonder onder aanbieding van Eede, verklaerden waar ende waeragtig te wesen, dat hun onderhebbende bodem gecalfaet, en van het verder vereijscht werdende, voor zoo veel men heeft opgegeven en verzogt als benodigt hebbende, mitsgaders alhier te missen is geweest, naer tijds gelegentheijd behoorlijk besorgt en voorsien, ook de garniering zodanig belegt is geworden, dat zij in het allerminste geen swarigheijt maken, om sComp:s goederen en principael den Canneel, die zij betuijgen wel geconditioneerd binnen scheeps „boort gekregen te hebben, met gerustheijt mede te nemen, als mede dat de provisien, in zo verre zijli: die voor de reijse alhier hebben ontfangen, goed, deugsaem en leverbaer zijn geweest. Eijndigende hier mede de attestanten hunne gegevene verklaring, die zij betuijgen te behelsen de opregte en suijvere waerheijt, gevende voor redenen van wetenschap als in den text, overzulx bereijt blijvende het geattesteerde nader met Eede gestant te doen Aldus gedaan ende gepasseert binnen de Ho gale, ter Secretarije van politie en justitie, ten dage, maend en jare voorsz:, ter presentie van hendrik Brakel en Cornelis Smittenberg Clercquen als getuijgen, die de minute dezes nevens de attestanten, en mij Eerste gesw: Com hebben onderteekent T welk getuijgt. „de Ey Clercq
text_translated_detailed: Today the 27th of November in the year 1751. There appeared before me Gerrit De Vos, bookkeeper and First sworn Clerk of this Castle Commandment, present the undersigned witnesses, namely: the Honorable Jan Willemszoon van den Briel, Captain Lieutenant, and Benjamin Carool, lieutenant, both in those capacities examined on the Indian bay, the seaworthy return ship Zuiderburg [Zuiderburg], which together and each of them individually, under the offering of an oath, declared to be true and truthful, that their vessel underneath had been caulked, and with regard to what further was required, insofar as it had been requested and asked for as being necessary, and also what was lacking here, according to the circumstances of the time had been properly taken care of and provided, and also the rigging had been arranged in such a manner that they in the least do not make any difficulty about taking the Company's goods and principally the cinnamon, which they testify to have received in good condition within the ship's hold, with peace of mind, as well as that the provisions, insofar as they have received them here for the voyage, have been good, suitable, and deliverable. Ending hereby the attestants their given declaration, which they testify to contain the upright and pure truth, giving as reasons for knowledge as in the text, whereupon remaining ready the attested matter to be confirmed further with an oath. Thus done and passed within the High Castle, at the Secretariat of Police and Justice, on the day, month, and year aforesaid, in the presence of Hendrik Brakel and Cornelis Smittenberg, Clerks as witnesses, who the original of this together with the attestants and me, First sworn Clerk, have signed. Which testifies. "the E. Clerk

Wij hebben het geluk gehad, per de scheepen Zuijderburg en De voorsigtigheid het Eerste als een voorzeijlder van de Ceilonse retour besending den 29. november anno preterito uijt dees bhaij vertrocken; en het laetste sijnde een bengaals retourbodem, dog mits bekomen schaede aan de boegspriet dees plaetse aangedaan, en na voorsiening van Een nieuwe d:o de reijse van hier hebbende ge-re-entameert, aan Uwel Edele Gestrenge hoog Achtb: aftevaerdigen, onse gants onderdanig letteren van den 29. ' november voormelt, en 6: deser lopende maend, waar van Copia afschrift de vrijheid gebruiken, desen telaten 28 versellen, die in submissie gerigt werd ten geleijde van de retourbodems hier beseijden met namen vermeld, dewelke 127 ingevolge het g'agt bevel van den wel Edelen agtb: heer raed Extra ordinaris van nederlands India en Ceilons Gouverneur Gerrard Ioan Vreelandt Nevens Den Raedt tot Colombo alhier geladen sijn, met de volgende goederen teweeten kisten packen en en vaten balen 120. – p. s ruw grof guinees - - - - - - 4. ƒ 1130. 10. —. 5130. –. „. gebl: grof guinees. - - . . . . 171. „. 48018. 2. 8. 1280. –. „. ruw grof Salmpoeris. - - 16. „. 5405. 8. 8. 6640. – „. gebl: grof Salmpoeris. . . 83. „. 28433. 18. —. 900. –. „. gebl: Callamaganijs. . . . . 9. „ 5180.
text_translated_detailed:
Original. To the Most Noble and Esteemed Gentlemen Philips van der Ghiessen, Josua van der Poorten, and Leendert Bomme, Representatives of His Most Serene Highness, the Prince of Orange and Nassau, and the Noble and Most Esteemed Gentlemen, the Directors at the Assembly of the Seventeen, representing the General Dutch East India Company at the Presidential Chamber Amsterdam, by the Return Ships Bloemendaal and Saamslag. Most Noble, Esteemed, and Most Honored Gentlemen, Wise, Prudent, and Most Generous Sirs!

We have had the good fortune that, by the ships Zuijderburg and The Foresight, the first having departed as a forerunner of the Ceylon return shipment on the 29th of November of the year past from this bay, and the last being a Bengal return vessel, but having sustained damage to the bowsprit at this place, and after provision of a new one, having re-embarked for the journey from here, we are dispatching to Your Most Noble and Esteemed Most Honored Gentlemen our most humble letters of the 29th of November aforementioned and the 6th of the current month, of which we take the liberty to provide copies herein, numbered 28, which were directed in submission as accompaniment to the return vessels mentioned by name here beside, which 127 according to the esteemed command of the Most Noble and Esteemed Councilor Extraordinary of Dutch India and Governor of Ceylon Gerard Joan Vreelandt, together with the Council at Colombo here, have been loaded with the following goods, namely chests, packages, and barrels, bales 120. – pieces of raw coarse guineas – 4. ƒ 1130. 10. —. 5130. –. „. bleached coarse guineas. – 171. „. 48018. 2. 8. 1280. –. „. raw coarse Salmpoeris [a type of cloth]. – 16. „. 5405. 8. 8. 6640. –. „. bleached coarse Salmpoeris. – 83. „. 28433. 18. —. 900. –. „. bleached Callamaganijs [a type of cloth]. – 9. „. 5180.

To the Well-born Noble Gentlemen Philips van der Ghiesen, Josua van der Poorten and Leendert Bomme Representatives of His Serene Highness, the Lord Prince of Orange and Nassau.

text_translated_detailed:
The Return Ship Blomedaal

I undersigned Hendrik Taal, Captain Lieutenant at sea in the service of the Esteemed Company and in that capacity appointed on the Return ship (which God Almighty be pleased to preserve, named Blomendaal) promise by these presents to properly administer all such ship's necessities; provisions, ammunition, and equipment of war, as well as whatever else is noted on the inventory of said vessel, and besides that which here on Gale is still provided for the journey toward the Fatherland according to the expense account of the same and the people assigned to it, signed by me, to keep good record of the consumption and what is worn out or otherwise becomes unusable in service of the Esteemed Company, and is lost, and to keep proper notation thereof in the books and the same together with the remainders thereof and defective weapons, thus such as more might be, with Love in the Patria coming to account to the Noble Honorable Gentlemen Directors of the general Dutch chartered East India Company at the Chamber Amsterdam or to those whom the said gentlemen shall be pleased to qualify for that purpose, to the fulfillment of which I bind my person and having good security with the Esteemed Company, together with all my goods both movable and immovable nothing excepted this deed is made hereof and signed by me two, one running bond documents Gale the 14th of January in the year 174[2]. Hendrik Taal

I undersigned Hendrik Taal, Captain Lieutenant at sea acknowledge by these presents that on behalf of the under my command the Return ship Blomendaal for the journey toward the Fatherland with all necessary items according to the circumstances of the time, both at Colombo and at this place, have been properly and orderly provided, and moreover the hull of all defects has been properly repaired and to my knowledge to the satisfaction of the aforesaid two points nothing is lacking:

text_original: Heeden den 14: Januarij 1752. —. Compareerden voor mij Gerrit Devos boekhouder en Eerste gesw: Clercq deses Jaaesen Commandements, Present denaarbesz: getuijgen D'E: Hendrik Taal Capitain lieutenant terzee, en Sijmon van Daalen opperstuurman. beijde in die qualiteijten bescheijden op het in dees baaij zeijlrheede leggend Retourschip Bloemendaal, dewelke tesamen en een ieder van hen in het bijsonder, onder aanbieding van eede, verclaarden waar ende waaragtig tewesen; dat hun onderhebbende Bodem gecalfaat en van het verder verEijscht werdende voor zo veel men heeft op gegeven en versogt als benodigt hebbende, mitsgaders alhier kennissen is geweest, naar tijds gelegentheid behoorlijk besorgt en voorsien, en ook de garniering zodanig belegt is geworden dat zij in het allerminste geen swarigheijd maken, om 'sComp=s goederen en principaal den canneel, die zij betuijgen wel geconditioneerd binnen scheeps boord gekregen tehebben met gerustheid mede tenemen, als mede dat de provisien in zo verre zijlieden, die voor de reijse alhier hebben ontfangen, goed, deugtsaam en leverban zijn geweest. Eijndigende hiermede de attestanten hunne gegevene verklaring, die zij betuijgen te beheezen de opregte en zuijvere waar „heijt, gevende voor reeden van wetenschap als inden text, over zulx bereijt blijvende het g'attesteerde nader met Eede gestand te doen. — Aldus gedaan ende Gepasseert in o stad gale, ten dage maand en Iaare voorsz: ter Presentie van Cornelis Blaauw „kamer, en Elias Theodorus Baptisl Clercquen als Getuijgen; die de minute deses, nevens de attestanten, en mij Eerste getw: 1657 Clercq hebben ondertekent Selk Getuijgt. — E Clece G de Nos LgClerg
text_translated_detailed: Today the 14th January 1752. —. There appeared before me Gerrit Devos bookkeeper and First sworn Clercq of this Year's Commandment, Present the aforementioned witnesses D'E: Hendrik Taal Captain lieutenant at sea, and Sijmon van Daalen chief steersman. both in those capacities examined on the Return ship Bloemendaal lying at anchor in this bay, which together and each of them individually, under the offering of oath, declared to be true and truthful; that their underlying Vessel had been caulked and from the further that was required, insofar as one has provided and requested as was necessary, likewise here it has been known, according to the circumstances of the time properly cared for and provided, and also the stowage has been arranged in such a way that they in the least make no difficulty, to take the Company's goods and principally the cinnamon, which they testify to have received in good condition within the ship's hold with peace of mind, as well as that the provisions insofar as they, which for the voyage here have received, have been good, suitable and deliverable. Ending hereby the attestants their given declaration, which they testify to possess the upright and pure truth, giving as reason for knowledge as in the text, over which remaining ready the attested further with Oath to stand. — Thus done and Passed in o city gale, on the day month and Year aforesaid: in the Presence of Cornelis Blaauw "chamber, and Elias Theodorus Baptisl Clercquen as Witnesses; who the minute of this, together with the attestants, and me First sworn 1657 Clercq have signed Such Witness. — E Clece G de Nos LgClerg

text_original: Retour Schip Spanderswout Ik Ondersgesz: Pieter Tornboom schipper in dienst der E: Comp: en in die qualiteijd bescheijden op 't schip /: Dat god almagtig gelieve te bewaren :/ genaamt Spanderswout beloove bij desen alle zodanige scheeps behoeftens, provisien ammonitie en Gereedschappen van oorlogen mitsgaders wat er meer zij als op den jnventaris van gedagte bodem genoteerd staad, en buijtendien het geene hier op Gale, nog voorderijse naar 't vaderland volgens onkost reek: aan deselve en daar op varende volk is verstrekt, door mij ondertekend behoorlijk te administreren van de Consumptie, en het geene ten dienste der E: Comp:s versleeten of anders onbruijkbaar word en weg „raakt goede aantekeningen daar van boek tehouden en 't selve nevens de restanten van dien of en de vencive wapenen dus danig wat dies meer mogte wesen met lief in 't patria komende te overhandigen aan de Edele agtb: heeren bewindhebberen der generale nederland „sche geoctroijeerde Oostindische Comp: ter Kamer Amsterdam ofte wel aan de geene die gem: heeren majores daar toe zullen gelieven te qualiciceeren tot naarkominge van 't welke verbinde, ik mijn persoon en bij de E: Comp: te goed hebbende gagie benevens alle mijne goederen zoo roerende als onroerende niets uijt gesondert des te oirkonde zijn hier van gemaakt en door mij ondertekend twee Eens luijdende verbandschriften Gale Den 25:' Januarij Anno 1752. text_translated_detailed: Return Ship Spanderswout. I, the undersigned Pieter Tornboom, skipper in the service of the Honored Company and in that capacity appointed to the ship (may Almighty God be pleased to preserve it) named Spanderswout, do hereby promise to properly administer all such ship's necessities, provisions, ammunition, and war equipment, as well as whatever else is noted in the inventory of said vessel, and furthermore whatever has been provided here at Gale and further on toward the fatherland according to the cost account for the same and the crew sailing thereon, as signed by me, properly to administer the consumption thereof, and that which is worn out or otherwise becomes unusable in the service of the Honored Company's affairs and is lost, to keep good records thereof in the books, and the same together with the remaining items thereof and the offensive weapons, thus such and whatever else might be the case, upon arrival in the fatherland to hand over to the Noble and esteemed gentlemen directors of the general Netherlands chartered East India Company at the Amsterdam Chamber, or else to those whom the aforementioned gentlemen majores shall be pleased to qualify for this purpose. To the fulfillment of which I bind myself, my person, and the salary I have with the Honored Company, together with all my goods, both movable and immovable, nothing excepted. In witness whereof two identical bond documents have been made and signed by me. Gale, the 25th of January, Anno 1752. Pieter Törnbohm. Return Ship Spanderswout. EE: Pieter Tornbhom schipper D. en Christiaan Hagerop opperstuurman beide in die qualiteiten bescheijden op het in dees baaij zijlvaardig leggende retourschip spaanders wout dewelke tesamen en een ieder van hen in het bijsonder, onder aenbieding van eede verclaarden waar ende waragtig teweesen, dat hun onderhebbende bodem gecalfaat en van het verder vereijscht werdende, voor zo veel men heeft opgegeven en versogt, als benodigt hebbende, mitsg:s alhier ternissen is geweest naer d tijds gelegentheijt behoorlijk besorgt en voorsien, en ook de garniering zodanig belegt is geworden, dat zij in het allerminste geen swarigheijt maken, om 'sComp:s goederen betuijgen wel geconditioneerd binnen 8die zij scheeps boord gekregen te hebben: net gerustheijt meede eneemen als meede dat de provisien in zo verre zijlieden die voor de reijse alhier hebben ontfangen goed, deugtzijn gesaam en leverbaar „weest. hiermeede de attestanten hunne Eijndigende gegevene verclaring die zij betuijgen te behelsen de opregte en suijvere waarheijt gevende voor reeden van wetenschap als in den text over zulx berijdbleijvende het g'attestee nader met Eede gestand te doen. Aldus Gedaan Ende gepasseert in deste gale ten dage maand en Jaare voorsz ter presentie van Cornelis Blaeuwkan en Elias Theodorus Baptist Clercquen als getuijgen die de minute deses nevens attestanten en mij Eerste gesw: Clercq hebben ondertekent Welk Getuijgt EGClercq J de Vos
text_translated_detailed: Today the 24th of January in the year 1752, there appeared before me Gerrit de Vos, bookkeeper, First sworn Clerk of this Galley, Commander and Resident, present as witnesses up to 6, namely: the Honorable Pieter Thornholm, skipper, and Christiaan Hagerop, chief steersman, both in those capacities described, concerning the return ship Spanderswout [Spanderswood] lying ready to sail in this bay, which together and each of them individually, under the offering of an oath, declared to be true and genuine, that the hull under their charge has been caulked and provided with everything further required, insofar as it has been requested and sought, as much as was necessary, with the assistance of those here in the harbor, and has been properly cared for and provisioned according to the circumstances of the time, and also the rigging has been arranged in such a manner that they in the least make no difficulty in testifying that the Company's goods have been received in good condition aboard the ship, and that they can take them with confidence, and also that the provisions insofar as they have received them here for the voyage are good, wholesome, and deliverable. Hereby the attestants conclude their given declaration, which they testify to contain the upright and pure truth, giving their reason for knowledge as in the text concerning which the attested matter remains to be confirmed with oath. Thus done and passed in this galley on the day, month, and year aforesaid in the presence of Cornelis Blaeuwkan and Elias Theodorus Baptist Clerck as witnesses, who have signed the original of this together with the attestants and myself, First sworn Clerk. Which testifies E.G. Clerck J. de Vos

Brief Summary of the Entire Cargo of the Four Return Ships Mentioned, namely:

Amsterdam, for the Chamber:
Return ship Suijderburg [Suiderburg] - ƒ287,494. 3. 8. [modern equivalent: Dutch guilders, shillings, and pence]
Bloemendaal - ƒ262,427. 15. -
Spanderswout - ƒ215,066. 15. —
Total: ƒ764,988. 13. 8.

For the Chamber Zeeland:
Saamslag - ƒ240,710. 13. -
Spanderswout - ƒ140,035. 9. 8.
Total: ƒ380,746. 2. 8.

Grand Total: ƒ1,145,734. 16. —

Further Summary of the Last Departing Ship Spanderswout:
For the Chamber Amsterdam: ƒ215,066. 15. —
For the Chamber Zeeland: ƒ140,035. 9. 8.
Total: ƒ355,102. 4. 8.

Now follows the brief accounting of the crew who are not to be repatriated on the return ship Spanderswout, namely 112 men in total, of which: 98 able-bodied sailors, 8 soldiers, 3 invalids, 2 passengers, 1 for provisions with deducted wages.

The 24th of January in the year 1752.
Galley A. Horpels.
